claim: Telomeres are crucial for cancer progression.
source: Telomeres are crucial for cancer progression.
evidence: This is a general statement in the abstract that draws from established scientific knowledge about telomeres and cancer.

claim: Immune signalling in the tumour microenvironment has been shown to be very important in cancer prognosis.
source: Immune signalling in the tumour microenvironment has been shown to be very important in cancer prognosis.
evidence: This statement references established knowledge in the field about immune signaling and cancer prognosis.

claim: The mechanisms by which telomeres might affect tumour immune response remain poorly understood.
source: However, the mechanisms by which telomeres might affect tumour immune response remain poorly understood.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge in the field, indicating a gap in understanding.

claim: Interleukin-1 signalling is telomere-length dependent in cancer cells.
source: Here, we observed that interleukin-1 signalling is telomere-length dependent in cancer cells.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study, supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Non-telomeric TRF2 binding at the IL1R1 promoter is affected by telomere length.
source: Mechanistically, non-telomeric TRF2 (telomeric repeat binding factor 2) binding at the IL-1-receptor type-1 (IL1R1) promoter was found to be affected by telomere length.
evidence: This is a mechanistic finding from the study, supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Enhanced TRF2 binding at the IL1R1 promoter in cells with short telomeres directly recruited the histone-acetyl-transferase p300.
source: Enhanced TRF2 binding at the IL1R1 promoter in cells with short telomeres directly recruited the histone-acetyl-transferase (HAT) p300, and consequent H3K27 acetylation activated IL1R1.
evidence: This is a mechanistic finding supported by ChIP-qPCR data in Figure 4 and HAT assay data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D.

claim: H3K27 acetylation activated IL1R1.
source: Enhanced TRF2 binding at the IL1R1 promoter in cells with short telomeres directly recruited the histone-acetyl-transferase (HAT) p300, and consequent H3K27 acetylation activated IL1R1.
evidence: This is a mechanistic finding supported by ChIP-qPCR data showing H3K27ac enrichment at the IL1R1 promoter in Figure 4.

claim: TRF2-mediated IL1R1 activation altered NF-kappa B signalling.
source: This altered NF-kappa B signalling and affected downstream cytokines like IL6, IL8, and TNF.
evidence: This is supported by western blot data showing NF-kappaB phosphorylation in Figure 6A-B and gene expression data in Figure 6C-D.

claim: TRF2-mediated IL1R1 activation affected downstream cytokines like IL6, IL8, and TNF.
source: This altered NF-kappa B signalling and affected downstream cytokines like IL6, IL8, and TNF.
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data showing expression of IL6, IL8, and TNF in Figure 6C-D.

claim: IL1R1 expression was telomere-sensitive in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) clinical samples.
source: Further, IL1R1 expression was telomere-sensitive in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) clinical samples.
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data from TNBC tissue samples shown in Figure 7F.

claim: Infiltration of tumour-associated macrophages (TAM) was sensitive to the length of tumour cell telomeres.
source: Infiltration of tumour-associated macrophages (TAM) was also sensitive to the length of tumour cell telomeres and highly correlated with IL1R1 expression.
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data showing TAM infiltration in TNBC samples with different telomere lengths in Figure 8B.

claim: TAM infiltration was highly correlated with IL1R1 expression.
source: Infiltration of tumour-associated macrophages (TAM) was also sensitive to the length of tumour cell telomeres and highly correlated with IL1R1 expression.
evidence: This is supported by the correlation between IL1R1 expression and TAM infiltration observed in TNBC samples.

claim: IL1 Receptor antagonist (IL1RA) could abrogate M2 macrophage infiltration in TNBC tumour organoids.
source: The use of both IL1 Receptor antagonist (IL1RA) and IL1R1 targeting ligands could abrogate M2 macrophage infiltration in TNBC tumour organoids.
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data showing reduced M2 macrophage infiltration in organoids treated with IL1RA in Figure 8E.

claim: IL1R1 targeting ligands could abrogate M2 macrophage infiltration in TNBC tumour organoids.
source: The use of both IL1 Receptor antagonist (IL1RA) and IL1R1 targeting ligands could abrogate M2 macrophage infiltration in TNBC tumour organoids.
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data showing reduced M2 macrophage infiltration in organoids treated with G4-binding ligand JD83 in Figure 8F.

claim: Gradual shortening of telomeres with cell division leads to cellular senescence/death.
source: Gradual shortening of telomeres and change in the telomeric structure with cell division leads to cellular senescence/death, which is crucial for tissue homeostasis (Jacobs, 2013; Karlseder et al., 2002; Shay and Wright, 2000).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Telomere shortening mediated cellular senescence is bypassed during oncogenic transformation.
source: During oncogenic transformation, the telomere shortening mediated cellular senescence is bypassed - resulting in uncontrolled cell proliferation and cancer progression; underlining the impact of telomeres in cancer (Blackburn, 2000; Hanahan and Weinberg, 2000; Maciejowski and de Lange, 2017; Paeschke et al., 2010; Shay, 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Shortening of telomeres with ageing contributes to compromised immune response.
source: Shortening of telomeres with ageing contributes to compromised immune response (Goronzy et al., 2006; Hodes et al., 2002; Pawelec et al., 2014; Sansoni et al., 2008; Weng, 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: How telomeres influence tumour immune response is poorly understood.
source: However, despite its relevance in cancer prognosis and intervention (Artandi and DePinho, 2010; Aviv et al., 2017; Chew et al., 2012; Balkwill and Mantovani, 2001; Greider, 1998; Hanahan and Weinberg, 2011; Wang et al., 2017), how telomeres influence tumour immune response is poorly understood.
evidence: This statement indicates a gap in current knowledge, supported by citations showing the relevance of the topic.

claim: TAMs predominantly promote immunosuppressive tumour microenvironment through secretion of anti-inflammatory cytokines.
source: TAMs – typically M2 macrophage-like – predominantly promote immunosuppressive tumour microenvironment (TME) through secretion of anti-inflammatory cytokines (Burkholder et al., 2014; Cassetta et al., 2016; DeNardo and Ruffell, 2019; Gonzalez et al., 2018; Pittet et al., 2022; Jayasingam et al., 2019), implicating the role of TAMs in aggressive tumour growth (Hu et al., 2016; Pittet et al., 2022).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Poor prognosis in triple-negative breast cancers has been frequently associated with TAMs.
source: Poor prognosis in triple-negative breast cancers (TNBC; negative for estrogen receptor [ER-], progesterone receptor [PR-], and HER2 receptor [HER2-]) has been frequently associated with TAMs (Wang et al., 2022; Yuan et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: M2-like TAMs are the most abundant monocytic immune cells in TNBC.
source: Multiple reports show M2-like TAMs to be the most abundant monocytic immune cells in TNBC and implicate their role in invasiveness and aggressive tumour growth (Burkholder et al., 2014; Jeong et al., 2019; Mantovani and Locati, 2013; Medrek et al., 2012; Oner et al., 2020; Chen et al., 2005; Yuan et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Telomere elongation led to differential expression of genes associated with innate immunity.
source: Seimiya. H and colleagues noted that telomere elongation led to differential expression of genes associated with innate immunity (Hirashima et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Telomere length of cancer cells is associated with immunity-related genes in colorectal cancer.
source: A published work on colorectal cancer showed the association of TL of cancer cells to immunity-related genes (Lopez-Doriga et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Telomere maintenance by Telomerase and ALT mechanisms led to alteration of TAM markers like CD163 in glioblastomas.
source: Another recent article showed that telomere maintenance by Telomerase (the key enzyme responsible for telomere maintenance) and ATL (alternative telomere lengthening) related mechanisms led to alteration of markers of TAM like CD163 in glioblastomas (Hung et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: TRF2 alters gene expression in a telomere length-dependent fashion.
source: We have reported earlier that the telomeric protein TRF2 alters gene expression in a TL-dependent fashion (Mukherjee et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement refers to the authors' previous work.

claim: TRF2 associates with gene promoters throughout the genome independent of its telomere-specific functions.
source: TRF2, although primarily a telomere-binding protein, was found to associate with gene promoters throughout the genome independent of its telomere-specific functions (Mukherjee et al., 2019a; Simonet et al., 2011; Yang et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work including the authors' own.

claim: TRF2 is sequestered at telomeres in cells with relatively longer telomeres.
source: Interestingly, TRF2 was sequestered at the telomeres and away from gene promoters in cells with relatively longer telomeres, and vice-versa in the case of cells with shorter telomeres.
evidence: This statement describes the telomere-sequestration-partition model from the authors' previous work.

claim: TRF2 occupancy at the IL1R1 promoter was significantly reduced in cells with long telomeres relative to short telomere cells.
source: TRF2-ChIP in ex vivo cultured HT1080-LT/HT1080 cells showed that TRF2 occupancy at the IL1R1 promoter was significantly reduced in cells with long telomeres relative to short telomere cells (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: IL1R1 mRNA expression was significantly lower in HT1080-LT relative to HT1080 cells.
source: IL1R1 mRNA expression was significantly lower in HT1080-LT relative to HT1080 cells (Figure 1B) conforming to the RNA-seq data described earlier (Figure 1—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1B and RNA-seq data in Figure 1—figure supplement 2D.

claim: IL1R1 protein was lower in HT1080-LT cells.
source: We found that the IL1R1 protein was also lower in HT1080-LT cells (flow cytometry; Figure 1C; western blot in Figure 1—figure supplement 2I).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 1C and western blot data in Figure 1—figure supplement 2I.

claim: Expression of IL1R1 at the cell surface was significantly lower in HT1080-LT compared to HT1080 cells.
source: Consistent with this, expression of IL1R1 at the cell surface was significantly lower in HT1080-LT compared to HT1080 cells (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Xenograft tumours from HT1080-LT cells had higher mean telomere length than those from HT1080 cells.
source: We found that the xenograft tumours from HT1080-LT cells had higher mean telomere length than those from HT1080 cells and had lower IL1R1 expression at the protein level (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Xenograft tumours from HT1080-LT cells had lower IL1R1 expression at the protein level.
source: We found that the xenograft tumours from HT1080-LT cells had higher mean telomere length than those from HT1080 cells and had lower IL1R1 expression at the protein level (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: TRF2 occupancy was lower in HT1080-LT-derived xenograft tumours.
source: It was observed that TRF2 occupancy (Figure 1F), as well as IL1R1 mRNA (Figure 1G) expression, was lower in HT1080-LT-derived xenograft tumours.
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: IL1R1 mRNA expression was lower in HT1080-LT-derived xenograft tumours.
source: It was observed that TRF2 occupancy (Figure 1F), as well as IL1R1 mRNA (Figure 1G) expression, was lower in HT1080-LT-derived xenograft tumours.
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1G.

claim: hTERT-inducible HT1080 cells gradually increased telomeres by ~50% over 12 days following hTERT induction.
source: Telomere-dependent TRF2 binding at the IL1R1 promoter was further checked using hTERT-inducible HT1080 cells that gradually increased telomeres by ~50% over 12 days following hTERT induction (Figure 1H, Figure 1—figure supplement 2K):
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data showing telomere length in Figure 1H.

claim: Gradual reduction of IL1R1 promoter TRF2 binding occurred with telomere elongation over 12 days in hTERT-inducible HT1080 cells.
source: gradual reduction of IL1R1 promoter TRF2 binding (Figure 1I) and IL1R1 expression (Figure 1J) with telomere elongation over the 12 days was notably consistent with observations made using HT1080/HT1080-LT cells (Figure 1A and B).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 1I.

claim: Gradual reduction of IL1R1 expression occurred with telomere elongation over 12 days in hTERT-inducible HT1080 cells.
source: gradual reduction of IL1R1 promoter TRF2 binding (Figure 1I) and IL1R1 expression (Figure 1J) with telomere elongation over the 12 days was notably consistent with observations made using HT1080/HT1080-LT cells (Figure 1A and B).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1J.

claim: MDAMB-231-LT cells have ~1.8- to twofold increase in telomere length.
source: In the resulting MDAMB-231-LT cells with ~1.8- to twofold increase in TL (Figure 1—figure supplement 2L), IL1R1 promoter TRF2 occupancy and IL1R1 expression were significantly lower (Figure 1K and L).
evidence: This is supported by telo-qPCR data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2L.

claim: IL1R1 promoter TRF2 occupancy was significantly lower in MDAMB-231-LT cells.
source: In the resulting MDAMB-231-LT cells with ~1.8- to twofold increase in TL (Figure 1—figure supplement 2L), IL1R1 promoter TRF2 occupancy and IL1R1 expression were significantly lower (Figure 1K and L).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 1K.

claim: IL1R1 expression was significantly lower in MDAMB-231-LT cells.
source: In the resulting MDAMB-231-LT cells with ~1.8- to twofold increase in TL (Figure 1—figure supplement 2L), IL1R1 promoter TRF2 occupancy and IL1R1 expression were significantly lower (Figure 1K and L).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1L.

claim: TRF2 over-expression increased IL1R1 mRNA expression and protein in HT1080 cells.
source: TRF2 over-expression (Flag-TRF2) showed an increase in IL1R1 mRNA expression and protein, and TRF2 silencing reduced IL1R1 in HT1080 cells (Figure 2A, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A) indicating that TRF2 activated IL1R1 expression.
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data in Figure 2A and western blot data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: TRF2 silencing reduced IL1R1 in HT1080 cells.
source: TRF2 over-expression (Flag-TRF2) showed an increase in IL1R1 mRNA expression and protein, and TRF2 silencing reduced IL1R1 in HT1080 cells (Figure 2A, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A) indicating that TRF2 activated IL1R1 expression.
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data in Figure 2A and western blot data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: TRF2 DNA binding is necessary for IL1R1 activation.
source: Flag-tagged TRF2-full-length, or a truncated version of flag-tagged TRF2 protein without the necessary domains for DNA binding (N-terminal Basic-domain [TRF2-delB] or C terminal MYB-domain TRF2-delM), showed that both TRF2 occupancy and IL1R1 promoter activity was compromised in case of the mutants; indicating TRF2 DNA binding as necessary for IL1R1 activation (Figure 2B and C).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-qPCR data in Figure 2B and luciferase reporter assay data in Figure 2C.

claim: Upon induction of TRF2, IL1R1 expression was enhanced in doxycycline-inducible TRF2 HT1080 cells.
source: We developed a doxycycline-inducible TRF2 model using HT1080 cells. Upon induction of TRF2, IL1R1 expression was also enhanced (Figure 2D and E).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data in Figure 2D and flow cytometry data in Figure 2E.

claim: IL1R1 expression at the cell surface was significantly higher in cells with higher TRF2.
source: We checked and found that IL1R1 expression of the cell surface was also significantly higher in cells with higher TRF2 (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: TRF2-induced tumours had enhanced IL1R1 relative to xenograft tumours where TRF2 was not induced.
source: HT1080 cells with doxycycline-inducible-TRF2 were used to make tumour xenografts in NOD-SCID mice. TRF2-induced tumours had enhanced IL1R1 relative to the xenograft tumours where TRF2 was not induced (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data from xenograft tumours shown in Figure 2G.

claim: Two G4 structures are present within the IL1R1 promoter TRF2-binding site.
source: Here, we found two G4s within the IL1R1 promoter TRF2-binding site (Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by sequence analysis shown in Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The DNA sequences of the G4 motifs formed G4 structures in solution.
source: We confirmed that the DNA sequences formed G4 structures in solution and specific base substitutions disrupted the structure formation (Figure 3B);
evidence: This is supported by circular dichroism data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Specific base substitutions disrupted G4 structure formation.
source: We confirmed that the DNA sequences formed G4 structures in solution and specific base substitutions disrupted the structure formation (Figure 3B);
evidence: This is supported by circular dichroism data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Both G4 forming motif sequences showed the characteristic Circular Dichroism signatures for 'parallel' G-quadruplex structures.
source: both G4 forming motif sequences showed the characteristic Circular Dichroism signatures for 'parallel' G-quadruplex structures which were largely abrogated when the sequences were mutated (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is supported by circular dichroism data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: BG4 antibody ChIP was enriched ~200 bp upstream on the IL1R1 promoter in HT1080 cells.
source: BG4 antibody [against G4s (Biffi et al., 2013)] ChIP was enriched ~200 bp upstream on the IL1R1 promoter in HT1080 cells (Figure 3C);
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: TRF2-dependent IL1R1 promoter activity was significantly compromised on introducing G4-deforming G>T substitutions on both G4 motifs.
source: TRF2-dependent IL1R1 promoter activity was significantly compromised on introducing G4-deforming G˃T substitutions on both the G4 motifs (Figure 3D), while the effect of the mutation was more for G4 motif B.
evidence: This is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The effect of G4-deforming mutation was more for G4 motif B.
source: TRF2-dependent IL1R1 promoter activity was significantly compromised on introducing G4-deforming G˃T substitutions on both the G4 motifs (Figure 3D), while the effect of the mutation was more for G4 motif B.
evidence: This is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: In the presence of the intracellular G4-binding ligand 360 A, TRF2 occupancy was significantly reduced at the IL1R1 promoter.
source: In the presence of the intracellular G4-binding ligand 360 A (Granotier et al., 2005), the TRF2 occupancy in HT1080 cells was found to be significantly reduced at the IL1R1 promoter consistent with results from other TRF2 binding sites (Mukherjee et al., 2019a; Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Upon treatment of HT1080 cells with 360 A, TRF2-induced IL1R1 promoter activity was significantly reduced.
source: Upon treatment of HT1080 cells with 360 A, TRF2-induced IL1R1 promoter activity, and expression/protein were significantly reduced (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is supported by luciferase reporter assay, qRT-PCR, and western blot data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: TRF2-dependent promoter activity from the inserted IL1R1 promoter-reporter was reduced when the G4 motif B was mutated.
source: Using CRISPR, we artificially inserted an IL1R1 luciferase-reporter-cassette (–1500 bp) at the CCR5 safe-harbour locus in HEK293T cells; TRF2-dependent promoter activity from the inserted IL1R1 promoter-reporter and TRF2 binding was reduced when the G4 motif B was mutated supporting earlier results (Figure 3F and G).
evidence: This is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: TRF2 binding was reduced when the G4 motif B was mutated in the artificially inserted IL1R1 promoter.
source: Using CRISPR, we artificially inserted an IL1R1 luciferase-reporter-cassette (–1500 bp) at the CCR5 safe-harbour locus in HEK293T cells; TRF2-dependent promoter activity from the inserted IL1R1 promoter-reporter and TRF2 binding was reduced when the G4 motif B was mutated supporting earlier results (Figure 3F and G).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 3G.

claim: CRISPR-mediated G>T editing in the G4 motif within the endogenous IL1R1 promoter resulted in a reduction of TRF2 binding.
source: Furthermore, CRISPR-mediated G>T editing in the G4 motif (motif B) within the endogenous IL1R1 promoter resulted in a reduction of TRF2 binding and IL1R1 expression (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and D).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: CRISPR-mediated G>T editing in the G4 motif within the endogenous IL1R1 promoter resulted in a reduction of IL1R1 expression.
source: Furthermore, CRISPR-mediated G>T editing in the G4 motif (motif B) within the endogenous IL1R1 promoter resulted in a reduction of TRF2 binding and IL1R1 expression (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and D).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1D.

claim: IL1R1 promoter H3K27 acetylation increased on TRF2 induction in HT1080 cells.
source: In both HT1080 and MDAMB-231 cells, IL1R1 promoter H3K27 acetylation increased/reduced on TRF2 induction/silencing respectively (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: IL1R1 promoter H3K27 acetylation reduced on TRF2 silencing in HT1080 cells.
source: In both HT1080 and MDAMB-231 cells, IL1R1 promoter H3K27 acetylation increased/reduced on TRF2 induction/silencing respectively (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: IL1R1 promoter H3K27 acetylation increased on TRF2 induction in MDAMB-231 cells.
source: In both HT1080 and MDAMB-231 cells, IL1R1 promoter H3K27 acetylation increased/reduced on TRF2 induction/silencing respectively (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: IL1R1 promoter H3K27 acetylation reduced on TRF2 silencing in MDAMB-231 cells.
source: In both HT1080 and MDAMB-231 cells, IL1R1 promoter H3K27 acetylation increased/reduced on TRF2 induction/silencing respectively (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: p300 occupancy at the IL1R1 promoter increased in TRF2-up conditions in HT1080 cells.
source: ChIP-qPCR confirmed p300 occupancy within upstream 200–400 bp promoter of IL1R1 in TRF2-up conditions, which reduced significantly on TRF2 downregulation, in HT1080 and MDAMB-231 cells (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: p300 occupancy at the IL1R1 promoter reduced significantly on TRF2 downregulation in HT1080 cells.
source: ChIP-qPCR confirmed p300 occupancy within upstream 200–400 bp promoter of IL1R1 in TRF2-up conditions, which reduced significantly on TRF2 downregulation, in HT1080 and MDAMB-231 cells (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: p300 occupancy at the IL1R1 promoter increased in TRF2-up conditions in MDAMB-231 cells.
source: ChIP-qPCR confirmed p300 occupancy within upstream 200–400 bp promoter of IL1R1 in TRF2-up conditions, which reduced significantly on TRF2 downregulation, in HT1080 and MDAMB-231 cells (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: p300 occupancy at the IL1R1 promoter reduced significantly on TRF2 downregulation in MDAMB-231 cells.
source: ChIP-qPCR confirmed p300 occupancy within upstream 200–400 bp promoter of IL1R1 in TRF2-up conditions, which reduced significantly on TRF2 downregulation, in HT1080 and MDAMB-231 cells (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Occupancy of acetylated-p300/CBP was enriched at the IL1R1 promoter on TRF2-induction in HT1080 cells.
source: Furthermore, occupancy of acetylated-p300/CBP (activated HAT) was enriched at the IL1R1 promoter on TRF2-induction in HT1080 cells (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: IL1R1 promoter occupancy of p300 was relatively low in HT1080-LT compared to HT1080 cells.
source: IL1R1 promoter occupancy of p300, CBP, ac-p300/CBP and H3K27ac was relatively low in HT1080-LT compared to HT1080 cells with shorter telomeres (Figure 4D) consistent with lower TRF2 occupancy at the IL1R1 promoter in LT cells (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: IL1R1 promoter occupancy of CBP was relatively low in HT1080-LT compared to HT1080 cells.
source: IL1R1 promoter occupancy of p300, CBP, ac-p300/CBP and H3K27ac was relatively low in HT1080-LT compared to HT1080 cells with shorter telomeres (Figure 4D) consistent with lower TRF2 occupancy at the IL1R1 promoter in LT cells (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: IL1R1 promoter occupancy of ac-p300/CBP was relatively low in HT1080-LT compared to HT1080 cells.
source: IL1R1 promoter occupancy of p300, CBP, ac-p300/CBP and H3K27ac was relatively low in HT1080-LT compared to HT1080 cells with shorter telomeres (Figure 4D) consistent with lower TRF2 occupancy at the IL1R1 promoter in LT cells (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: IL1R1 promoter occupancy of H3K27ac was relatively low in HT1080-LT compared to HT1080 cells.
source: IL1R1 promoter occupancy of p300, CBP, ac-p300/CBP and H3K27ac was relatively low in HT1080-LT compared to HT1080 cells with shorter telomeres (Figure 4D) consistent with lower TRF2 occupancy at the IL1R1 promoter in LT cells (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: TRF2 directly interacts with p300.
source: We found that TRF2 directly interacted with p300, evident from co-immunoprecipitation using lysate from HT1080 cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Transfer of the acetyl group to histone H3 was significantly enhanced in the presence of both TRF2 and p300.
source: To ascertain direct TRF2-p300 interaction and consequent H3K27 acetylation, we did histone-acetyl-transfer assays using purified p300, histone H3, and acetyl-CoA (substrate for the acetyl group) with or without recombinant TRF2. Transfer of the acetyl group to histone H3 was significantly enhanced in the presence of both TRF2 and p300, relative to p300 only; and TRF2 co-incubated with p300 without H3 gave marginal HAT activity (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is supported by HAT assay data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D.

claim: TRF2-K293R gave notably compromised activation of IL1R1 at mRNA levels.
source: TRF2-K293R gave notably compromised activation of IL1R1 at mRNA and protein levels (Figure 5B–D).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: TRF2-K293R gave notably compromised activation of IL1R1 at protein levels.
source: TRF2-K293R gave notably compromised activation of IL1R1 at mRNA and protein levels (Figure 5B–D).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data in Figure 5C and immunofluorescence data in Figure 5D.

claim: The binding of flag-TRF2-293R at the IL1R1 promoter was similar to TRF2-WT.
source: The binding of flag-TRF2-293R at the IL1R1 promoter was similar to TRF2-WT (Figure 5E) suggesting that the loss in IL1R1 activation was not due to lower promoter binding by TRF2-293R.
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: TRF2-293R significantly reduced p300 recruitment on the IL1R1 promoter relative to TRF2-wildtype induction.
source: However, TRF2-293R significantly reduced p300 and ac-p300/CBP recruitment on the IL1R1 promoter relative to TRF2-wildtype (WT) induction (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: TRF2-293R significantly reduced ac-p300/CBP recruitment on the IL1R1 promoter relative to TRF2-wildtype induction.
source: However, TRF2-293R significantly reduced p300 and ac-p300/CBP recruitment on the IL1R1 promoter relative to TRF2-wildtype (WT) induction (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: TRF2 mutant K293R showed lower physical interaction with p300 in comparison to TRF2 WT.
source: TRF2 293R also showed lower physical interaction with p300 in an immunoprecipitation experiment in comparison to TRF2 WT (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: dCas9-TRF2-K293R diminished IL1R1 levels in HT1080 cells.
source: On using sgRNA against the IL1R1 promoter, we found significant activation or downregulation of IL1R1 in the case of dCas9-TRF2 or dCas9-TRF2-K293R, respectively, in HT1080 and MDAMB231 cells.
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: dCas9-TRF2-K293R diminished IL1R1 levels in MDAMB231 cells.
source: On using sgRNA against the IL1R1 promoter, we found significant activation or downregulation of IL1R1 in the case of dCas9-TRF2 or dCas9-TRF2-K293R, respectively, in HT1080 and MDAMB231 cells.
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: dCas9-TRF2 showed activation of IL1R1 in HT1080 cells.

claim: Median telomere length in TNBC samples was ~3.6 kb.
source: We measured TL (telomere length) in tissues from 94 breast cancer (TNBC) patients: Median TL was ~3.6 kb (quantitative-telomeric-RTPCR; O'Callaghan et al., 2008; Telo-qPCR-see Materials and methods; Figure 7A, Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This is supported by telo-qPCR data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Telomere length difference between TNBC-ST and TNBC-LT was clear using TelSeq analysis.
source: Further, reads from the whole genome sequence of the TNBC samples were analyzed for estimation of TL using the reported pipline- TelSeq (Ding et al., 2014): TL difference between TNBC-ST and LT was clear, and cancer tissue had lower TL than adjacent normal tissue consistent with earlier reports (Aviv et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by TelSeq analysis data shown in Figure 7C.

claim: Cancer tissue had lower telomere length than adjacent normal tissue.

evidence: This is supported by TelSeq analysis data shown in Figure 7C.

claim: About ~70% or more TNBC samples showed lower telomere length in tumour samples compared to adjacent normal tissue.

evidence: This is supported by telo-qPCR and TelSeq data shown in Figure 7D.

claim: EpCAM+ve cells within the TME had significant heterogeneity in telomere length.
source: EpCAM+ve (tumour-cell marker; Went et al., 2004) cells within the TME had significant heterogeneity in TL (lower in TNBC-ST vis-a-vis LT), whereas the difference in TL of EpCAM-ve cells was insignificant indicating TL variation in TME was primarily from cancer cells (Figure 7E, Figure 7—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 7E.

claim: The difference in telomere length of EpCAM-ve cells was insignificant.

evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 7E.

claim: Telomere length variation in TME was primarily from cancer cells.

evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that EpCAM+ve cells show TL heterogeneity while EpCAM-ve cells do not.

claim: Telomerase activity negatively correlated with telomere length in TNBC.

evidence: This is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1C.

claim: TERC was found to be significantly enhanced in TNBC-LT samples.

claim: TERC is possibly a more important determinant for telomere length in TNBC.

evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that TERC, but not TERT, was significantly different between long and short telomere TNBC samples.

claim: Overall patient survival was significantly lower in IL1R1 high samples.
source: We, next, used publicly available TCGA gene expression data of breast cancer samples (BRCA; Supplementary file 4) to assess the effect of IL1R1 expression on cancer prognosis. We categorised samples based on IL1R1 expression: IL1R1 high (N=254) and IL1R1 low samples (N=709). Notably, overall patient survival was significantly lower in IL1R1 high samples (Log-rank p value: 0.0149; Figure 7—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This is supported by survival analysis of TCGA data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1G.

claim: Metaplastic breast cancer was only found within the IL1R1 high samples.
source: We also checked the frequency of occurrence of various breast cancer sub-types in IL1R1 high and low samples (Figure 7—figure supplement 1H). While invasive mixed mucinous carcinoma (the most abundant sub-type) was predominantly seen in IL1R1 low samples, metaplastic breast cancer was only found within the IL1R1 high samples.
evidence: This is supported by frequency analysis shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1H.

claim: Metaplastic breast cancer has been frequently found to be 'triple negative'.
source: Interestingly, metaplastic breast cancer has been frequently found to be 'triple negative', that is ER-, PR-, and HER2- (Reddy et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: MRC1 was the most significantly upregulated marker in IL1R1 high samples.
source: When breast cancer transcriptomic data from TCGA was segregated into high and low IL1R1 groups (Supplementary file 4). Within the differentially expressed genes between high and low IL1R1 groups, we looked at key immune markers such as reported TAM markers (CD163, MRC1,D86,CD80), TAM chemo-attractants (CCL2, CCL3,CCL5, CCL8,CXCL12; Unver, 2019) as well as reported TIL markers (CD3G, CD4,CD8A, FOXP3,ENTPD1, PDCD1; Figure 8A, Supplementary file 5). We found that MRC1 (gene coding for CD206-M2 macrophage marker) was the most significantly upregulated marker in IL1R1 high samples.
evidence: This is supported by differential gene expression analysis shown in Figure 8A.

claim: TERT was found to be significantly downregulated in IL1R1 high samples.
source: Interestingly, TERT (often correlated/associated with high telomere length; Greider, 1998; McNally et al., 2019) was found to be significantly downregulated in IL1R1 high samples.
evidence: This is supported by differential gene expression analysis of TCGA data.

claim: TNBC-LT had relatively low TAM infiltration compared to TNBC-ST.
source: Nine TNBC-ST and nine TNBC-LT tumours were analyzed for M2-type TAMs by double-positive CD11b (monocyte-derived cells; Cassetta et al., 2016) and CD206 (M2-specific; Jaynes et al., 2020) labelling: TNBC-LT had relatively low TAM infiltration (mean 1.78%, range: 0.18–5.41%) than TNBC-ST (mean 7.34%, range: 3.76–16.80%; Figure 8B; Figure 8—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 8B.

claim: CD206 expression was lower in tissue sections from TNBC-LT relative to TNBC-ST tumours.
source: Accordingly, CD206 expression was found to be lower in tissue sections from TNBC-LT relative to TNBC-ST tumours (Figure 8C).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 8C.

claim: The total proportion of immune cells did not vary significantly between short and long telomere TNBC samples.
source: We further found that the total proportion of immune cells (% of CD45 +ve) did not vary significantly between short and long telomere TNBC samples (Figure 8—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1C.

claim: TNBC-ST samples had a higher percentage of myeloid cells within the CD 45+ve immune cell population.
source: However, TNBC-ST samples had a higher percentage of myeloid cells (CD11B+ve) within the CD 45+ve immune cell population.
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data showing CD11B+ve cells in CD45+ve population.

claim: The percentage of M1 macrophages in the myeloid population did not vary significantly between TNBC-ST and TNBC-LT samples.
source: We checked in three TNBC-ST and TNBC-LT samples and found that the percentage of M1 macrophages (CD86 high CD 206 low) in the myeloid population was lower than that of the M2 macrophages (CD 206 high CD 86 low) and unlike the latter, did not vary significantly between TNBC-ST and TNBC-LT samples (Figure 8—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1C.

claim: TNBC-ST had higher M2-type macrophage infiltration compared to TNBC-LT in patient-derived organoids.
source: TAM infiltration was further tested using patient tumour-derived organoids from five long and five short telomere cases. M2-type macrophage derived from THP1 cells (Figure 8—figure supplement 1E) were labelled (red-tracker dye) before co-incubating with each of the five TNBO-ST or five TNBO-LT: Following 12 hr incubation TNBO-ST had on average 8.56% infiltration of M2-type macrophages (range: 6.54–10.9%) compared to 3.14% (range: 0.99–4.88%) for TNBO-LT (Figure 8D).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data from organoid infiltration assays shown in Figure 8D.

claim: Organoids treated with IL1RA showed >50% reduction in macrophage infiltration.
source: Organoids treated with IL1RA before co-incubating with dye-labelled M2-type macrophages showed >50% reduction in macrophage infiltration (Figure 8E).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data from organoid infiltration assays with IL1RA treatment shown in Figure 8E.

claim: JD83 is effective in reducing IL1R1 expression at 5 µM concentration in TNBO.
source: These ligands were tested in TNBO and we found JD83 to be effective in reducing IL1R1 expression at 5 µM concentration (Figure 8F).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 8F.

claim: JD83 is effective in reducing M2 migration in TNBO.
source: We found that JD83 is also effective in reducing M2 migration in TNBO, showing promise for future therapeutic interventions.
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data from organoid infiltration assays with JD83 treatment shown in Figure 8F.
